{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of agreement (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values) between animal model results (rat, large animal) and human clinical outcomes for hemodynamic effects of compounds.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "Cardiovascular (CV) safety pharmacology studies are conducted to identify these safety effects. Understanding translation of CV endpoints (specifically, heart rate [HR], and blood pressure [BP]) across preclinical animal models and to the clinic is critical in developing a robust CV derisking strategy.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Cardiovascular (CV) safety-related attrition is an important contributor to the loss of promising drug candidates during development.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "we investigated translation of HR and BP endpoints using data from 83 compounds that were tested in telemetry studies in rat and large animal (LA; dog or monkey) and 79 compounds that were tested in LA telemetry studies and human phase I clinical trials.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "data from 83 compounds that were tested in telemetry studies in rat and large animal (LA; dog or monkey)",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Sensitivity, specificity as well as predictive values were calculated for rat to LA model comparison and for LA to human studies comparison."
}
